full_judgment:
"Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 8-2-2018 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Satkhira in Civil Revision No. 31 of 2014 rejecting the revision and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 4-8-2014 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Syamnagor, Satkhira in Title Suit No.77 of 2014 rejecting the application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying operation of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 322 of 1984 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, inter alia, that in Title Suit No. 77 of 2014, the plaintiff-petitioners filed an application for staying the preliminary decree dated 6-6-1984 passed in the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984. Upon hearing, the learned Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge) was pleased to reject the stay petition. Impugning the judgment and order of the learned Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), the plaintiff-petitioners preferred a Revisional Application being No. 31 of 2014 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Satkhira. After admitting the said revisional application, the learned District Judge transferred the same to the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Satkhira for disposal. Upon hearing, the learned Additional District Judge was pleased to reject the said revisional application. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and order of the learned Additional District Judge, Satkhira, the petitioners moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule and stay therewith. 

 3. Mr Abul Kalam Azad, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that in Title Suit No. 77 of 2014, the plaintiff-petitioners filed an application for staying the preliminary decree dated 6-6-1984 passed in the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984. But unfortunately, the learned Senior Assistant Judge without applying his judicial mind and without considering the ratio decided by the Apex Court of the country most illegally rejected the said stay petition and eventually, the learned Additional District Judge, without any independent assessment of the facts and circumstances of the case, most illegally rejected the same and thereby committed an error of law causing serious prejudice to justice. He further submits that if the preliminary decree is not stayed the purpose of filing Title Suit No. 77 of 2014 will be frustrated and it will cause serious prejudice to the plaintiff-petitioners. Ile finally submits that the plaintiffs of the Title Suit No. 77 of 2014 were not parties to the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984 and therefore, they could not contest the said partition suit and, as such, the Rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 5. Per contra, Mr Sheikh Habib-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the Senior Assistant Judge after considering facts and circumstances of the case rightly dismissed the petition for staying the operation of the preliminary decree dated 6-6-1984 passed in the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984 and the learned Additional District Judge after assigning cogent reason was pleased to concur with the order of the learned Senior Assistant Judge and therefore, the concurrent findings of the Courts below do not warrant for any interference and, as such„ the Rule is liable to be turned down to secure the ends of justice. 

 7. The learned Senior Assistant Judge held that with the knowledge of the predecessor of the petitioners, the preliminary decree of the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984 was passed; therefore, the application for staying the further proceeding of the aforesaid suit invoking section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 could not be stayed till disposal of the Title Suit No. 77 of 2014. The learned Additional District Judge rightly concurred with the decision of the learned Senior Assistant Judge with the following observation: 

 9. It appears from the record that the Partition Suit was decreed in preliminary form on 6-6-1984 and it is yet to be made final and the Advocate Commissioner was appointed to make partition as per preliminary decree. It also appears from the record that the defendant No. 29 was the predecessor of the plaintiffs of the Title Suit No. 77 of 2014. The aforesaid petition for staying the further proceeding of the Title (Partition) Suit No. 322 of 1984 after more than 38 years is unfounded and baseless; rather it is a device to prolong the litigation so that the plaintiffs cannot enjoy the fruits of long cherished preliminary decree. 1 strongly hold that such an application is a machination and procrastination on the part of the petitioners with an ulterior motive. By filing a suit, the petitioners cannot acquire any right to staying the process of making the preliminary decree as final as a matter of course or luxury unless there is sufficient cause to do the same. The finding of the learned Additional District Judge is based on sound reasoning and his tailor made judgment agreeing with the penultimate decision of the learned Senior Assistant Judge is immune from any interference. Hence, the Rule shall fall through as it is devoid of any substance.
